phrase: NEWS ITEMS FROM LAST WEEK: “We have to humanize the machine to give it social purpose by directing our energies towards the reconstruction of our inner world,” said Walter Gropius, Harvard professor of Architecture on Monday evening in his second address at Black Mountain College.

“We expect the city of tomorrow to stretch its borders much farther than it does today, dissolving at the same time its chaotic conglomerations of incoherent functions and piled-up building masses into smaller units.
It is ironic that were people live closest together today their social life is thoroughly disintegrated.
The communal life in today’s cities is destitute.
“Thus the artist of today can rise above imitation, above the holding of the mirror up to nature.
He recreates his own bounds and brings about an artistic order, an order much more strict than is evident in the world today.

phrase: WITH FORMER STUDENTS: In the Mail: PFC Henry Adams writes from Austria on May 8: “As I sit here writing this letter, the BBC is coming in over the radio with program after program celebrating V-E Day.
Today they are in a situation that I’m only too grateful to be out of myself.

Though they were all young, none over 25, their faces were lined and tired, and they looked ten years older than their years..Today they are all heading home...No doubt, the German PW’s over there are being put on trains for the long ride back to Germany.
